title: Children and faith
hook: teach them diligently, talking on the way (Deuteronomy 6:7)
tomorrow: what did Jesus arrange for his mother at the very end?

segments.voice: A week of the year and the people in it, in six lines: come; come apart awhile; walk to pray; remember whose you are; faithful in much; and yesterday, love begins at home. Today, one more, for the youngest people at the table.
screen: `LOVE BEGINS AT HOME.` → `SIX LINES, AND ONE MORE.`

segments.voice: From the back seat, between a snack and a song: where was I before I was born? Or: does God sleep? Kids ask the biggest questions at the worst times, at a red light, half-asleep at bedtime, while you're looking for parking. A very old book saw that coming. It doesn't say to wait for a classroom. It says to talk on the road.
screen: `A QUESTION FROM THE BACK SEAT.` → `AT THE WORST TIMES.` → `TALK ON THE ROAD.`

segments.voice: Here are the words, from a book Christians and Jews both read: “And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.” Notice where it starts: in thine heart. What's passed on is first what's lived. Then the places: the house, the road, bedtime, morning. Ordinary hours. Faith here gets taught in the cracks of the day more than at a desk. In the Gospels, when the disciples push children away, Jesus says: “Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.” Suffer here means allow. And for the back seat, a psalm even answers one of those questions: “Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.” Here's one to tell a friend: an honest I don't know, said kindly on the way, teaches too. Not everyone has children at home; godparents, aunts, older cousins and neighbors pass faith on as well.
screen: `FIRST, IN THINE HEART.` · `SITTING, WALKING, LYING DOWN, RISING.` · `LET THEM COME.` · `NEITHER SLUMBER NOR SLEEP.` · then, large: `ON THE WAY.`

segments.voice: Say Deuteronomy's four times out loud, slowly, one on each breath: sitting, walking, lying down, rising up. On each one, let a face come to mind: a child, a niece, a kid down the street, or the child you once were. Stay with whoever comes.
Children and faith. Faith passed on in ordinary hours, in the house and on the way, and it starts in the heart.
Your line: on the way. Seven lines this week, and this one fits in a car. A week, done.

screen: `DAY 1715 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 34 OF 70.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DID JESUS ARRANGE FOR HIS MOTHER AT THE END?`

howItsDone: Christian families pass on faith in many shapes: bedtime prayers, grace at meals, a Bible story in the car, a question answered honestly; godparents, grandparents and church teachers share the work.

match.prompt: faith on the way — tap the pairs.
pairs: the road, the walk, the car

it names the house, the road, lying down and rising up.
in the KJV, 'suffer the little children' means let them come
"forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God."

fork.setup: a seven-year-old asks you at bedtime, "where's heaven?" you're honestly not sure. what fits Deuteronomy 6?
options: make up a confident answer so they feel safe.
say you're not sure, and wonder about it together.
tell them they're too young for that question.
fork.reveal: Deuteronomy puts the talking in ordinary hours, lying down included. what's passed on is what's lived, and an honest I don't know, said kindly, teaches too.

original.note: Hebrew: and thou shalt teach them diligently, Deuteronomy 6:7.

trapdoor: what you thought: teaching faith means lessons and a curriculum.
what it means: talking of it in ordinary hours, at home and on the way, starting in your own heart.
what a scholar hears: Deuteronomy 6 names sitting, walking, lying down and rising up, and begins with 'in thine heart'.
guess: passing faith on to children in the ordinary hours of life
a church class that teaches children Bible facts
a rule that kids must choose a faith by a set age

chat.says: driving my cousin eli to practice and he goes 'does God sleep?' i panicked and turned up the radio
options: Turn it down and ask what he thinks. Deuteronomy says talk of it on the way. Car rides count.
Tell him to save it for Sunday school, where a teacher can explain it properly.
Give him the full answer with verses, so he gets it exactly right the first time.
chat.meaning: Deuteronomy 6:7 puts faith-talk on the road and at bedtime. And a psalm has his answer: he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.

Deuteronomy.meaning: a book of the Torah, in the Old Testament

Gospels.meaning: the four books that tell Jesus' life

psalm.meaning: a sacred song from the Bible's book of Psalms

godparents.meaning: adults who promise to help raise a child in faith
